name: Bleeding Disorder Due to P2Y12 Defect

criteria.description: Presence of mucocutaneous bleeding symptoms such as epistaxis, easy bruising, or menorrhagia
Demonstration of impaired platelet aggregation response to ADP in platelet function assays
Identification of pathogenic variants in the P2RY12 gene
Normal coagulation factor levels and normal platelet count
Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance of bleeding symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical bleeding symptoms plus impaired platelet aggregation to ADP and identification of pathogenic P2RY12 variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other platelet function disorders and coagulation defects.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Impaired platelet aggregation response to ADP
searchTerms: platelets don't clump well with ADP

pathognomonic.notes: Includes epistaxis, gingival bleeding, and easy bruising
searchTerms: bleeding from skin and mucous membranes

common.notes: Heavy menstrual bleeding in affected females

occasional.notes: Joint bleeding less common than in coagulation factor deficiencies

occasional.symptomName: Prolonged bleeding after surgery or trauma
searchTerms: bleeding that lasts long after surgery or injury
prolonged bleeding after trauma or operation

rare.notes: Very rare but life-threatening bleeding complication
Blood in urine due to bleeding

laboratory: Impaired platelet aggregation in response to ADP
imaging: Imaging may be required to assess bleeding complications such as intracranial hemorrhage
other: Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Defect in platelet integrin αIIbβ3 rather than P2Y12 receptor
Absent platelet aggregation response to multiple agonists including ADP and collagen
Reduced secretion of ADP and other granule contents

redFlags: Severe mucocutaneous bleeding unresponsive to standard hemostatic measures
Intracranial hemorrhage or other life-threatening bleeding
Family history of unexplained bleeding disorders
references: Nurden AT. P2Y12 receptor defects: a new class of bleeding disorders. Platelets. 2014;25(3):195-201.
Orphanet: Bleeding disorder due to P2Y12 defect. ORPHA:36355.
Cattaneo M. Platelet P2 receptors: focus on P2Y12. J Thromb Haemost. 2015;13 Suppl 1:S10-6.
